observations: The historical terrain loader bounds and hashes the manifest and compressed pack, validates chunk metadata and ranges, and verifies decoded length, digest and discriminants lazily. Manifest geometry completeness, cache resource accounting and all malformed input paths remain to be traced.

Historical routing admits bounded profile and weather values at its public entry points, coarsens a geographic window to a node cap, uses a deterministic A* search and reconstructs compacted path and exposure spans. Arithmetic bounds, zero-distance and crossing semantics, deadline coverage, route simplification and consumers of the resulting spans require connected assessment.

The historical road package binds its source and full-precision geometry digest to a final terrain pack, bounds metadata and payload, rejects malformed tags/counts and converts checked coordinates to E7. It keeps classification in the payload while its geometry digest covers point lists; the intended identity of classification and native-to-presentation handoff need independent examination.
